# EEP 9999 - A fixture that passes every check

## Abstract

The known-good fixture. Every other file in this directory is this one
with a single rule broken, so that each rule is seen failing on its own
before it is trusted to pass.

## Motivation

A checker nobody has watched fail is a checker nobody has tested.

## Specification

This document conforms to every rule `tools/check-eeps` enforces, except
the one it is named for. When it stops doing so, a rule has changed and
the fixtures need regenerating.

### The pin

This fixture adopts nothing real. It names a revision in EEP 8's form so
that the rule has something to find, at revision
`0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567` of `docs/nothing.md` in
`github.com/example/nothing`, committed 18-Sep-2026.

There is no drift sentence after it and no substitution table below it,
which is what `E017` exists to refuse.

## Rationale

Holding the baseline in a file, rather than in the checker's own tests,
lets a reader see what a conforming EEP looks like without running
anything.

## How to teach this

Read this file. Then read one of its broken siblings and the rule it is
named for.

## Reference implementation

The first EEP written from the template without an editor's corrections.

## Rejected ideas

- Generating the fixtures at test time. A reviewer could not then read
  them in the diff.

## Open issues

None. A link written as inline code, such as
`![alt text](path)`, is an example and not a link, so M009 must
leave it alone.

A line carrying one long literal, such as
`PEP 13 | vacant. Until a governance EEP exists, the owner is the whole council`,
runs past 80 characters and must not be reported: rewrapping a literal would
change it. M005 exempts it only because the literal is what pushes it over.

## Acknowledgements

Written for the EEP checker.
